findings.title: Capping a derived PASS erases 919's verdict provenance, and the synthetic finding states something untrue in that case
findings.description: D4's rule fires on `verdict is PASS` with no condition on *how* that PASS was obtained, and D6 explicitly designs for the reachable combination "a PASS parsed with `fallback_used=True` … that then gets the synthetic finding." In that case `impose_diff_coverage` sets `verdict_source = IMPOSED` (D5), overwriting the `DERIVED` value slice 919 assigned — so the frontmatter no longer records that the model never stated a verdict, which is the entire contract `VerdictSource` exists for (`models.py` docstring: "Whether a review's verdict was stated by the model or derived"). Worse, the synthetic finding's fixed text asserts "The model's own verdict was PASS" in a run where no verdict was stated at all. D6 keeps the not-parsed *notice* alive but does not address the provenance field it displaces, nor make the finding text conditional. Fix by composing the two facts (e.g. digest/notice carries "verdict was derived, then imposed on", or the finding text keys on `fallback_used`) rather than letting IMPOSED silently replace DERIVED.

findings.title: D2's tri-state invariant is unreachable on the git-failure path — a diff that was requested but never measured records as "no diff"
findings.description: D2 states "`diff_injection` is `None` when `inputs` has no `diff` key … When a diff was part of the review, the key is always written." But `_inject_file_contents` (review_client.py:420-425) only measures the diff when `_run_git_diff` returns content; on `FileNotFoundError`/non-zero exit it returns `None` and the injection is skipped — a path that runs *after* `_run_git_diff_filenames` succeeded seconds earlier (same ref, both git calls), so the divergence is possible. In that state `inputs` **has** a `diff` key and `DiffInjection` is `None`, so per D2 the artifact omits `diffTruncated` and a gate reads the run as "no diff / nothing to judge" — precisely the silent-fact-loss this slice exists to fix, on an I/O failure path the slice re-purposes for a new consumer. D3 covers the one skip case `_add_injection` reports (total-limit → `injected_chars: 0`) but nothing defines the counts or presence for "diff requested, measurement impossible." Enumerate it explicitly: with a `diff` key present and no measured body, either record a defined state (e.g. `diff_chars: null`) or fail loudly — not absence, which D2 reserves for a run that had no diff request.

findings.title: "Two `review_client` call sites" for `_inject_file_contents` is wrong — there is one
findings.description: Step 2 of the Development Approach says to "Update its two `review_client` call sites." The whole file contains a single call (`prompt = _inject_file_contents(...)` in `run_review_with_profile`); the other listed updates are direct test-module calls, which the same sentence covers separately. Small, but this is a change-of-signature task where a wrong call-site count sends the implementer looking for a seam that does not exist.

findings.title: D6's render fix also changes artifacts outside the synthetic-finding case it justifies
findings.description: Moving the `fallback_used` notice from an `elif` to an unconditional post-findings render fixes the D6 scenario, but it also changes rendering for any pre-existing review that already produced `findings` non-empty with `fallback_used=True` — a latent condition that predates this slice. That is a correct fix and tiny, but it is a behavior change to every degraded artifact's body, not only to capped ones; worth one sentence in the CHANGELOG/SC list so snapshot expectations (`clean_pass_artifact.md` aside) aren't surprised.

findings.title: `aiModel`'s meaning change for OpenAI-dated judges is disclosed and reasoned, but nothing verifies metrology still resolves identities
findings.description: D10 correctly identifies the consumer (`metrology/identity.py` keys on frontmatter `aiModel`) and argues the new value is the right calibration identity. The claim in Integration Points that `aiModel`'s new meaning is "the meaning its consumers assumed all along" is evidenced for the SDK path (#134) but asserted, not verified, for OpenAI-direct judges whose values will change (`gpt-5` → `gpt-5-2025-08-07`). Add one walkthrough step or SC confirming metrology identity derivation still succeeds and that no consumer hard-codes the requested id under the `aiModel` key — D10's own consequence paragraph shows values will move.
